problem: Existing object-navigation world models are built only from past observations, so the agent cannot anticipate unseen areas. The few imaginative methods (ImagineNav, SGM) need task-specific training and use image or map representations that lack global semantic reasoning. Prior symbolic (scene-graph) methods are limited to a single floor.
motivation: Indoor environments follow semantic priors (bedrooms near bathrooms, stairs imply upper floors), and humans use these to anticipate unseen areas and find targets faster. Scene graphs are text-expressible, so they suit zero-shot VLM/LLM reasoning, which can complete unknown regions without training.
key_idea: Maintain a hierarchical object-region-floor scene graph and prompt a VLM to imagine (complete) the scene graph in unexplored regions, then choose frontiers by a fallback between semantic exploitation gain and raycast exploration gain.
insight: Imagination raises scene-graph recall at a small precision cost, and that trade is net-positive for navigation: SR 57.25 -> 62.50 in the module ablation (row b vs c), and GPT-4o-mini performs the same as GPT-4o. Combining exploitation and exploration gains adds a further +2.75 SR (c vs d). The floor level matters most (dropping it hurts most), and region-only semantics beat object+region, suggesting object-level cues are noisy. An oracle scene graph reaches 72.25 SR, so imagination quality still leaves headroom.
method: Symbolic world modeling: a bottom-up tree-structured scene graph (objects -> regions -> floors). Objects come from open-vocabulary detection (Grounded-SAM) lifted to 3D with depth and associated over time. Objects are grouped into regions by k-d tree neighbors with wall-crossing pruning, regions are captioned by CLIP against a room-type list, and a new floor node is added upon stair traversal.

Symbolic world imagination: unknown regions from the occupancy map plus the observed graph are projected to a BEV image, and a VLM (GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini) with layout-prior hints predicts region captions and typical objects for each unknown region. It runs asynchronously every 20 steps or on region changes, and the imagined graph is used only for gain estimation and never merged into the observed graph.
Context-aware goal verifier: a VLM checks a candidate target detection together with nearby objects and room context to reject false positives.
Target exploitation gain: the max semantic relevance (LLM query, alternatively CLIP) between the target and the object/region nodes in a local subgraph around each frontier.
Target exploration gain: discounted accumulated raycast visible-unknown area along the path to each frontier, normalized to 0-1.
Fallback frontier selection: pick the frontier with max exploitation gain if it exceeds threshold lambda (0.3), otherwise the one with max exploration gain.
3D planner: FMM on a 2.5D map (height map plus gradient) that treats stairs as traversable, plus a 3-stage stair-climbing routine for multi-floor search.

setting.backbone: Grounded-SAM detector, CLIP, GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini (frozen VLM for imagination and verification), Qwen2.5-7B (LLM scoring); all frozen
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions in Habitat, with frontier goals planned by FMM
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D, HSSD); Isaac Sim for the appendix large-scale comparison
setting.privileged: none (GT scene graph only in the oracle ablation)

numbers.extra: Strict success distance 0.1 m, 500 steps; baselines quoted with 1.0 m
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (main results): SGImagineNav HM3D SR 65.4, SPL 30.0

numbers_note: HSSD was tagged 'HSSD-ObjNav' and its split was not named in the paper (validation episodes assumed). The SPL-per-SR ordering is as printed, and the HM3D ablation SR/SPL are on a 400-episode subset.
results: SGImagineNav reaches 65.4 SR on HM3D and 66.8 SR on HSSD zero-shot, beating InstructNav (58.0), MFNP (58.3), and trained imaginative methods SGM (60.2) and ImagineNav (53.0). SPL is competitive (30.0, versus VLFM 30.3 and ProcTHOR 31.8). It also demonstrates cross-room and cross-floor search on a Go1 legged robot.
limitations: No sequential or long-term planning, so temporal redundancy remains.
Baselines are quoted from papers with a 1.0 m success radius while this paper uses 0.1 m, so the comparison is not identical; the SPL is not the best on HM3D.
Dependence on API VLM calls (about 6 s each) and perception errors (false positives, mapping, stair climbing); runtime is about 1.2 Hz.
